'''Dramassia''' was a densely-populated [[Ecumenopolis/Legends|urban planet]] located in the [[Dramassia system/Legends|Dramassia system]] of the [[Juvex sector/Legends|Juvex sector]], a part of the [[Senex-Juvex/Legends|Senex-Juvex]] region in the [[Western Reaches/Legends|Western Reaches]] portion of the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]]. It lay on the [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]] known as the [[Agarix Trade Route]], which connected it to the [[Pieldi system/Legends|Pieldi]] and [[Umthyg system/Legends|Umthyg systems]]. Dramassia was the point of origin of the [[Shimmersilk/Legends|material]]<ref name="TEA" /> known as [[Dramassian shimmersilk]],<ref name="RFU">''[[Rebel Force: Uprising]]''</ref> which was already encountered offworld<ref name="TOR" /> around [[3643 BBY]].<ref name="Date">Per the reasoning [[Template:TOR_dates|here]], Act I of ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'' takes place around [[3643 BBY]], and players of ''The Old Republic'' can obtain the [[Dramassian shimmersilk|Dramassian Silk]] Crafting Material independently of the main class storyline at any point during the game.</ref>

After the [[Colonist/Legends|settlement]] of the Senex-Juvex around [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]] by a group of [[Currency/Legends|affluent]] [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] inhabitants led by the enterpreneur [[Thull Vandron]], Dramassia became the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of [[House Halliikeenovich]], one of the [[Noble/Legends|aristocratic]] [[Ancient Houses]] that eventually came to rule over the region. The planet became one of the Juvex [[Sector/Legends|sector's]] economic powerhouses, manufacturing a wide range of products that included [[Silk/Legends|silk]] and [[Mining/Legends|mining]] equipment. However, the economic power of Dramassia was seen by the other Ancient Houses as somewhat unseemly, and House Halliikeenovich was perceived as greedy and grasping.<ref name="TEA" />

==Behind the scenes==
Dramassia was introduced in the [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', authored by [[Daniel Wallace]] and [[Jason Fry]], which placed it in grid square L-18.<ref name="TEA" />
